# A merge deliberately stops before the commit so the result can be reviewed, and
# the finalize refreshes the plaintext of everything the merge staged - otherwise
# a stale pre-merge file would be sealed back over what the merge brought in.
#
# That refresh must not reach a file the user edited in the very window the merge
# handed them. It tells the two apart by what the plaintext matches: the staged
# object (already the merge result), HEAD's object (never touched, stale), or
# neither (written by the user). Only the middle case is revealed.

sesam-repo admin base.txt ours.txt theirs.txt edited.txt

cp $TMPDIR/base.txt s
exec sesam add s --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add s'

# THEIRS changes the last line.
exec git checkout -b topic
cp $TMPDIR/theirs.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'topic: change last line'

# OURS changes the first line - a different region, so the driver merges both
# sides cleanly and reseals %A itself.
exec git checkout master
cp $TMPDIR/ours.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'ours: change first line'

! exec git merge topic
stderr 'no conflicts, resealed'
stderr 'merge changed the vault - run `git commit` to finalize'

# Both sides survived and there is nothing left to resolve - which status now says
# without inventing conflict markers to go and fix.
exec cat s
stdout 'OURS'
stdout 'THEIRS'
exec sesam status
stdout 'nothing to show - everything in sync'
stdout 'nothing left to resolve'
! stdout 'resolve the conflicted'

# The user tweaks the merged secret while reviewing, then finalizes.
cp $TMPDIR/edited.txt s
exec git commit -m 'merge topic'
stderr 'you changed 1 secret after the merge; sealing your version'
stderr 'sesam:   s'

# Their edit is what got sealed, not the driver's merge.
exec cat s
stdout 'MY-EDIT'
exec sesam show .sesam/objects/s.sesam
stdout 'MY-EDIT'

exec sesam verify
stderr 'Integrity: ok'
exec git status --short
! stdout .

-- base.txt --
line one
line two
line three
-- ours.txt --
OURS
line two
line three
-- theirs.txt --
line one
line two
THEIRS
-- edited.txt --
OURS
MY-EDIT
THEIRS
